review_notes: I read the whole file. It contains only two generated, noncomputable proof-certificate terms (`nb091SplitAlpha0003` and `nb091SplitAlpha0004`), one-off freshness lemmas (`nb091_focused_notmem_*`), one `TEnvFresh` chain (`nb091_compact_envfresh_0016`), one `TReflOn` wrapper (`nb091FocusedRefl0001`), and a few trivial `∉ ∅` lemmas (`nb091_compact_fv_empty_*`). It defines no new structure, class or inductive type, and no new notion that stands in for a Mathlib concept. The types it uses (`TAlphaWff`, `TEnvFresh`, `TReflOn`, `Class`, `Wff`, `freshVar`) come from upstream project files. They model a project-specific first-order class syntax with alpha-equivalence, and I found no Mathlib counterpart for them. The `∉ ∅` lemmas restate `Finset.notMem_empty`. That is standalone theorem duplication, which the rubric excludes. I did not open the upstream files that define `TEnvFresh` and `TAlphaWff`, so I cannot rule out an overlap there. Any such overlap would belong in those files and not in this one.
